newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Jan industrial output rises 5.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Jan industrial output rises 5.9 pct.

text.p: South Korea's industrial output in January rose 5.9 percent year-on-year, down from a 12.4 percent rise a year earlier, provisional National Statistical Office (NSO) figures showed on Friday.
NOTE: figures in percent, year-on-year change.
The NSO figures showed industrial output fell 1.7 percent in January from December 1996, against a 1.9 percent rise a year ago.
The month-to-month fall in output was due largely to labour unrest that hit the nation's major manufacturers, including the auto industry.
The labour strike lasted for nearly a month from late December in protest at the forced passage of a new labour law, that allows companies to lay off workers and replace strikers.
The NSO said vehicle output in January dropped 34.1 percent on the year, while garments and fur products fell 22.3 percent.

Output of heavy-industrial goods rose 8.6 percent year-on-year in January against a 15.2 percent rise a year ago, while that of light-industrial products fell 5.4 percent, against a rise of 2.7 percent.
The NSO figures showed ex-factory shipments for exports in the month increased 10 percent year-on-year, against a 24 percent rise a year before.
Shipments to the domestic market fell 0.3 percent, compared with a rise of 9.9 percent a year ago.
